general_information.Learning-Teaching Method: Project-based learning, Inquiry-based Teaching, Experiential learning methods
general_information.Description: The Circuit Design Project course aims to provide students with both theoretical understanding and practical experience in modern electronic circuit design. By the end of the course, students will be able to: - Understand and apply the modern electronic circuit design process — from requirement analysis, schematic design, and PCB layout to to manufacturing and hardware validation. - Demonstrate proficiency in Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools such as KiCad, Altium or Cadence OrCAD (optional), capable of designing and verifying single-layer and double-layer PCBs. - Integrate hardware and firmware (using MCU STM32/Nucleo; ESP32/ESP8266, Arduino...) to test and validate their hardware designs and circuit functionality. - Develop key engineering competencies including teamwork, communication, documentation, and project management aligned with industry practice. - Cultivate creativity and innovation by designing functional and application-oriented electronic products, with potential extensions in IoT, sensing, control, or embedded systems.
general_information.StudentTasks: Students are expected to: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Attend and participate actively in lectures, labs, and discussions according to the weekly schedule - Complete all project milestones, including: - Collaborate effectively in teams, including task allocation, maintaining project logs, and performing peer reviews of other teams’ designs - Engage in self-directed learning by exploring components, IoT modules, and best practices in EMC/EMI and layout optimization - Deliver and present the Final Project, including a functional PCB prototype, working firmware, a comprehensive technical report, and a live or recorded demonstration
general_information.Tools: - KiCAD (open-source EDA tool) - Devkit Nucleo F401Rx or Microcontroller unit - Components of MCP201 subject.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Analyze technical requirements to propose appropriate circuit system architectures and schematic solutions.
Design and verify electronic schematics, perform ERC checks, and generate netlists and BOMs for PCB implementation.
Create and optimize PCB layouts (single-layer and double-layer) that comply with DRC rules and basic EMC/EMI design principles.
Develop and test firmware on the STM32 microcontroller (or Nucleo board)/ESP32/Arduino UNO to validate hardware functionality.
Integrate peripheral and IoT modules into their circuit designs to build functional and application-oriented systems.
Prepare technical reports and deliver professional presentations, demonstrating engineering communication skills and project documentation competence.
